review: A real subprocess opens the native admitted SQL schema and existing routed Grafx graph, commits revision 2 and terminates with os._exit(73) at before_relational_ack after the actual fence and durability_applied checks. Reopening observes revision-2 graph relations, the claimed queue token/deadline and unchanged relational audit IDs. Revision 3 arrives while that claim exists. Existing stale-claim recovery and the real worker converge to revision 3 without duplicate relation/provenance/maturity tuples; another replay preserves the entire multiset.
native_storage: The opt-in native_schema test fixture uses initialize_current_schema/current_schema_contract on empty storage. Child and parent reopen through the normal format guard; no manual schema stamp, conversion or bypass.
timing: Only the crashed child writer's TTL is configured to an admitted 5 seconds, with normal ownership verification and heartbeat. The test waits 6 real seconds after termination before reacquiring. Claim recovery receives a clock at its persisted deadline+1 via the existing WorkerClockPort. No lease marker is deleted or bypassed.
failure_disposition: replay1: hook targeted a nested helper unavailable as a module attribute; process did not reach crash point.
replay2: ordinary reopen correctly refused the partial Base.metadata fixture. Switched this test to the official native initializer.

replay3: crash boundary and persisted graph/no-ACK assertions passed; immediate retry correctly refused the still-valid 300-second writer lease. Final test uses a short valid TTL and waits for actual expiration.
closure_reference: closure-native-main37.json; product and SPA unchanged since the byte proof and eight-zero-budget closure.
limits: One focused real-process crash proof; not a full HTTP/browser E2E campaign or every possible crash point.
Source changes are test fixtures; no new permission, policy or lifecycle authority.
